A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MUSE research despite the changed title. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, ensemble comparisons, case studies and parameter-sensitivity experiments on TruthfulQA, EHRShot and MIMIC-Extract.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds model-selection diagnostics and supervised fine-tuning experiments, including Tables 4, 9, 11 and 12.

M1.justification: The greedy and conservative MUSE algorithms remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 3.3 adds a substantial training extension: supervised fine-tuning with consensus or per-model probabilities, optionally combined with teacher-generated Original, Bayesian or no-probability chain-of-thought supervision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TruthfulQA, EHRShot and MIMIC-Extract prediction tasks. The new fine-tuning experiments reuse MIMIC-Extract LOS3; they change training procedures rather than introduce another dataset, domain or prediction task.

E2.justification: The original single-model, majority-voting and mean-aggregation comparators are retained. The added SFT comparisons introduce controls without the consensus probability and alternatives using raw per-model probabilities or different reasoning prompts (Tables 11–12). These comparator additions are confined to the new training extension.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a training-based evaluation protocol for Mistral-7B and Qwen2-7B on LOS3, with probability-input and reasoning controls. CoT data generation uses GPT-o3-mini and 300 training samples per setting. The original ensemble evaluation metrics, sampling temperature and generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine model-selection frequencies, removal of Mistral from the candidate pool, and individual-model divergence from the MUSE consensus (Tables 4 and 9). Tables 11–12 also test probability inputs and reasoning variants. The original sensitivity plots and weak-model case studies are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten stochastic generations and 100 bootstrap trials resampling 90% of outputs. v2 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All seven original result tables retain their entries and values: v1 Tables 1–7 correspond to v2 Tables 1–3 and 5–8. v2 adds selection frequencies, consensus JSD and extensive SFT results. For example, Table 11 reports Mistral default SFT with the consensus probability at 54.83 AUROC and 31.84 ECE under SLL; these are new training conditions, not revised original scores.

T1.justification: The definitions of epistemic disagreement, aleatoric entropy and combined uncertainty remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the SFT extension adds no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The original ensemble-calibration contribution remains. v2 substantially expands the stated contribution in its abstract, introduction and conclusion to investigate whether MUSE probabilities can supervise probabilistic reasoning in individual LLMs, reporting mixed, model-dependent outcomes.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of selection frequencies and consensus divergence to address whether MUSE merely excludes weak models. It also develops a new discussion of SFT benefits depending on model, probability representation and reasoning style, including calibration–discrimination tradeoffs. The original binary-task and deployment limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer, identifies the Azure GPT-o3-mini teacher, specifies 300 generated samples per setting, and supplies CoT prompt templates with a 200-word limit. The original hardware and quantization disclosures remain; detailed SFT optimizer and training-budget information is still absent.

R1.justification: The cited works and Related Work discussion are unchanged. The positioning against single-model uncertainty estimation and earlier multi-LLM fusion remains the same; the new SFT investigation does not develop an additional comparison with prior research.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates the former uncertainty-quantification and selection sections into Methods, organizes Results around two research questions, and moves the diversity/noise and adaptive-selection discussions into the appendix. It also changes the title and rewrites the conclusion around the expanded scope.

P2.justification: v2 adds an eight-panel SFT figure and Tables 4 and 9–12, covering diagnostics, boxed prompts and training results. The original contour figures are preserved as Figures 2–3, with the TruthfulQA plot moved into the appendix and the appendix layout substantially rearranged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful selection diagnostics, SFT controls, prompts and a code pointer. However, new calibration claims contain consequential metric mismatches: Appendix A.10 compares Mistral GEN BS ECE 16.63 against 28.37, which Table 6 identifies as baseline Brier; the actual baseline ECE is 15.63, reversing the claimed improvement. The retained ethics statement also says no fine-tuning occurred. These inconsistencies affect the principal new extension, making its benefits versus the loss of reporting reliability difficult to assess overall.
